ops.body:
Design detail for daemon boot and shutdown. Source keeps terse contracts; this is the why. (Rewritten 2026-07-19 for the daemonkit migration — the old exact-equality eviction, evictPeer ladder, and wg-only drain are gone.)

## Startup goroutine ordering (startupTable)
After listen() has bound the daemon socket and pre-accept sync setup has finished, serve launches one tracked startup-orchestrator goroutine and enters the accept loop without waiting for startup maintenance. Health is therefore available throughout startupTable execution.

The orchestrator invokes eligible startupTable rows sequentially; cancellation or closing stops the table, and gated rows may be skipped. The current order is:

session.heartbeat → bridge.content → bridge.fp → holder.refresh → ua.detect → fp.app.ensure → overlays.reconcile → content.coordinator

That ordering governs row invocation and return; several rows launch tracked asynchronous work that can continue after the row returns. Once the table returns with execCtx still live, the orchestrator starts the heal loop in a child goroutine and enters the scheduler itself.

The ordering constraints:
- within startupTable, the content-bridge and FP-bridge startup attempts precede overlays.reconcile, which can mount fuse rows and Check/Reconcile File Provider domains. Each bridge row waits only a bounded time for availability, so this is attempt ordering, not a guarantee that both bridges have bound; request-path work is accepted concurrently;
- holder.refresh primes the mount cache before startup reconciliation. A select racing the daemon-socket-bind→startup-prime gap calls mountReady, which refreshes a stale cache on miss before deciding;
- ua.detect runs after the daemon socket bind and after both bridge rows; it detects the Claude version and stamps the OAuth User-Agent;
- overlays.reconcile finishes before content.coordinator is started and before the heal loop and scheduler start. The content coordinator and heal loop can call overlay Reconcile, including fuse reconciliation; the scheduler runs pollTable and does not perform fuse Setup/Reconcile.

## listen() — single-entrant bind, takeover via daemonkit
Binds the unix socket (0600) under an exclusive flock on socket+".lock" (proc.SingleEntrant, held for the daemon's serving lifetime and NEVER removed — unlinking a held lock file would let a third daemon flock a fresh inode and reopen the race). The Evict closure is the only cc-pool policy: it runs daemonkit daemon.Run (RequestDaemon + SocketRelease, Grace = evictTimeout) behind the daemonPeer adapter — Health and the OpShutdown handshake over the daemon wire, with the victim pid read from the socket via Darwin getsockopt(LOCAL_PEERPID) (kernel-attested, not supplied by the lifecycle response), and takeover-only proto-TOLERANT reply decoding so a cross-proto incumbent takes the full ladder (public clients stay strict).

Policy is newer-wins: a strictly-newer arrival evicts (Shutdown → grace → re-Health with pid/start-time revalidation → SIGKILL); same-or-newer incumbent → ExitSelf, exit 0, and the LaunchAgent's KeepAlive {SuccessfulExit=false} keeps the loser down. A downgrade no longer evicts (the old any-skew rule is gone; dev sentinels still beat releases). A flock held without a bound socket is polled; if it remains held through the deadline, listen returns ErrLockStillHeld, not ErrPeerStarting.

## handle() — lifecycle ops before the proto gate
OpHealth and OpShutdown dispatch BEFORE the proto-version gate. They form the takeover lifecycle surface: a cross-proto Health returns the incumbent's version, and Shutdown initiates drain. Both bypass drain admission and stay on the serve waitgroup through their response write attempt. Work ops sit behind the proto gate and drain admission.

## serve() — settle-before-cancel drain
Shutdown first closes the daemon listener and the configured sync RPC listener to unblock their accept loops. After the daemon accept loop exits, serve runs drain.Simple: close admission, idempotently deactivate both listeners, settle admitted native work through its response write attempt and admitted sync work through handler return, mark the maintenance loops closing, then cancel executors. It then waits the serve waitgroup.

The executor context is context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx)); in production ctx is the outer signal context, so admitted work outlives shutdown signaling. New compatible work that reaches admission is refused. Run closes the store only after serve returns. Sync RPC response transmission occurs after its admitted handler returns and is not tracked by drain or the serve waitgroup.
